_meta.indication: MIPLYFFA is indicated for use in combination with miglustat for the treatment of neurological manifestations of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-month trial; patients randomized 2:1 to weight-adjusted MIPLYFFA or placebo three times daily, stratified by miglustat use.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 2 to 19 years of age with molecularly confirmed NPC and at least one neurological symptom at baseline.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary endpoint was change from baseline to month 12 in the 5-domain NPC Clinical Severity Scale (5DNPCCSS); for this resubmission a post hoc rescored 4-domain scale (R4DNPCCSS) change from baseline was used as the primary efficacy endpoint.
pivotal_trials.result: On the R4DNPCCSS (ANCOVA), estimated treatment difference -1.51 (95% CI: -2.95, -0.06; nominal p=0.0413) favoring arimoclomol; in the labeled miglustat subgroup the placebo-subtracted difference was -2.2 (95% CI -3.8, -0.6).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=15%) in MIPLYFFA-treated patients also receiving miglustat were upper respiratory tract infection (31% vs 15% placebo), diarrhea (23% vs 23%), and decreased weight (15% vs 0%). Serious adverse reactions were hypersensitivity reactions including urticaria and angioedema; mean increases in serum creatinine of 10% to 20% were observed.
target_moa: The precise mechanism by which arimoclomol exerts its clinical effect in NPC is unknown; the applicant proposed stabilization of HSF1 to enhance the heat shock response and upregulate heat shock proteins (e.g., HSP70) important in chaperone-mediated autophagy and lysosomal/autophagosome function.
modality: Small molecule (arimoclomol citrate, a new molecular entity)

advisory_committee.vote: Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee convened August 2, 2024; voted 11 Yes, 5 No, 0 Abstain that trial NPC-002 results in concert with the other data support that arimoclomol is effective in the treatment of patients with NPC.

summary.text: Arimoclomol received Orphan Drug, Fast Track, and Breakthrough Therapy designations and a Rare Pediatric Disease designation for NPC. FDA issued a complete response to the original NDA on June 17, 2021; the Applicant resubmitted on December 21, 2023, and the drug was granted traditional approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial (NPC-002) plus confirmatory evidence, together with a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

citations.quote: IND 124547 has received Orphan Drug Designation, Pediatric Rare Disease Designation, Fast Track Designation, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation. A more detailed summary of the regulatory history for IND 124547 is included the Appendix (Section 12).

In this resubmission, the Applicant is seeking traditional approval of arimoclomol based on the findings of study NPC-002 with a modified analysis of the primary endpoint as primary support for efficacy along with additional confirmatory evidence.
We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA.

requirement.text: PMC 4699-1 Conduct a clinical drug interaction trial to assess the effect of concomitant administration of arimoclomol on the pharmacokinetics (PK) of miglustat and the effect of concomitant administration of miglustat on the PK of arimoclomol. Design and conduct the trial in accordance with the FDA guidance for industry Clinical Drug Interaction Studies — Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions (January 2020).
